newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatari foreign minister receives Israeli letter.
newsitem.headline: Qatari foreign minister receives Israeli letter.

text.p: Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani on Sunday received a letter from his Israeli counterpart David Levy covering the Middle East peace process, the official news agency QNA said.
The letter also focused on bilateral ties. QNA gave no further details and did not say how the message was delivered.

It was the first publicly reported exchange since Sheikh Hamad met Levy in Cairo in November and told him Doha would not proceed with the planned opening of a trade mission in Israel unless there was progress in peace talks with the Palestinians.
Qatar and Oman have raced ahead of other Gulf Arab states in establishing economic ties with Israel but stopped short of diplomatic relations pending the resolution of the Arab-Israeli conflict.
The Jewish state has trade missions in the two countries, and Oman has opened a trade representation office in Tel Aviv.
Oman and Qatar said late last year they had put their contacts with Israel on ice to protest against hardline Israeli policies towards the Palestinians.
But they welcomed the January accord between Palestinian and Israeli leaders to expand Arab rule to the West Bank town of Hebron.
